title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Previous weeks at $12.03: 13 and 24 units (x0.70 and x1.29 vs baseline); price hike likely dampens demand, but effect is muted.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: No past data on TikTok trends; no historical precedent, but product is visible. Noise-adjusted effect from similar trends is uncertain. Evidence is weak.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. A 6.2% price increase to $12.03 is likely to reduce demand, but the product is trending on TikTok—unconfirmed by past data. Recent weeks show no promotion, but the 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks at $12.03 saw 13 and 24 units (x0.70 and x1.29 vs baseline), with no clear lift. The noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.4, but this is a price hike, not a discount. The TikTok trend is a new driver with no historical echo; confidence is low. No event or promotion, so classical model suggests x1.0. Adjust down slightly for price, up marginally for trend, but shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 3.6 - 38.4 | 10%-90%: 7.5 - 34.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
